newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says states may ask for original VAT invoices.
newsitem.headline: Court says states may ask for original VAT invoices.

text.p: The European Court of Justice decided on Thursday that member states have broad discretion over document production to determine the credibility of tax deductions.
A German citizen before the German finance court asked for the option of producing proof of qualified VAT deductions other than the original invoices.
The German court asked for a definition of invoice under the VAT directive and whether the taxpayer must produce originals to deduct input tax.

The court concluded "article 18(1)(a) and article 22(3) of the Sixth directive permit member states to regard as an invoice not only the original but also any other document serving as an invoice that fulfils the criteria determined by the member states themselves."

The court also said that member state rules imposed for the correct levy and collection of tax, and the prevention of fraud, may require original invoices but they also have the power, where the originals are unavailable, to admit other evidence proving a deductible transaction occurred.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Greek)
"Value added tax - Interpretation of article 18(1)(a) of the Sixth Council directive 77/388/EEC - Deduction of input tax paid - Obligation of the taxable person - Possession of an invoice"
Reference from the Bundesfinanzhof for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between

on the interpretation of article 18(1)(a) of the Sixth Council directive 77/388/EEC of 17 May 1977 on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment (OJ 1977 L 145, p. 1)

Article 18(1)(a) of the Sixth Council directive 77/388/EEC of 17 May 1977 on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment permit the member states to regard as an invoice not only the original but also any other document serving as an invoice that fulfils the criteria determined by the member states themselves, and confer on them the power to require production of the original invoice in order to establish the right to deduct input tax, as well as the power, where a taxable person no longer holds the original, to admit other evidence that the transaction in respect of which the deduction is claimed acutally took place.
